issues.subcategory: contradictory intervention timing
issues.description: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible accounts of when the resistance interventions occur: after collaborative recall, before collaborative recall, and again after collaborative recall in the procedure. This is not a minor procedural detail; the theoretical interpretation differs radically depending on timing. If administered before discussion, the intervention is a pre-exposure inoculation and may alter the discussion itself. If administered after discussion, it is a post-warning/source-monitoring intervention and cannot prevent social exposure to misinformation. The power analysis, causal interpretation, manipulation labels, and practical implications all depend on resolving this contradiction.
issues.quote: "In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below)." / "What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation)." / "The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material."

issues.subcategory: intervention would reveal deception if administered before discussion
issues.description: The extended warning is described as telling participants that the partner saw a different version and explaining the deception. If this is delivered before collaborative recall, as one part of the manuscript states, it destroys the MORI cover story, changes the social interaction, and makes the subsequent discussion qualitatively different from ordinary co-witness contamination. If delivered after collaborative recall, the stated inoculation rationale is false. Either way, the design needs a coherent timing and deception plan.
issues.quote: "Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied" / "What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase"

issues.subcategory: contradictory final-test format
issues.description: The manuscript alternates between saying the final memory test is open-ended and saying it is two-alternative forced choice. These formats measure different constructs, produce different base rates, require different scoring rules, and require different statistical models. The contradiction makes the primary dependent variable unclear and prevents evaluation or replication of the analysis plan.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie" / "First we will examine the memory conformity effect using the procedure of Garry et al. (2008; also Ito et al., 2019), but with modification concerning applying open-ended questions in the individual memory test." / "In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format."

issues.subcategory: counterbalancing contradiction
issues.description: The design claims that discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the procedure says every pair will discuss the same four critical details. If the same details are always discussed, discussion status is confounded with item identity, salience, memorability, and difficulty. The within-subject comparison of discussed versus non-discussed items would then not isolate misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: "In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced." / "In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase."

issues.subcategory: item confounding with misinformation condition
issues.description: Because only eight critical details exist and the same four are apparently always discussed, any accuracy difference between discussed and non-discussed details could reflect inherent item differences rather than memory conformity. For example, the discussed details may be more visually subtle, more confusable, or more memorable than the non-discussed details. Without item counterbalancing or item-level modeling, the central memory conformity estimate is biased.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details" / "each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase"

issues.subcategory: non-independence of dyadic observations
issues.description: Participants are nested in dyads and influence one another during discussion, yet the planned analysis treats participants as independent observations in a standard two-factor ANOVA. Outcomes from partners are mechanically and socially dependent because each participant's misinformation exposure is generated by the other participant. Ignoring dyadic clustering can produce underestimated standard errors, inflated Type I error rates, and incorrect power estimates. The analysis should account for dyad-level random effects or otherwise use dyad as the unit of analysis.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." / "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels"

issues.subcategory: power analysis ignores dyadic clustering
issues.description: The power analysis uses the number of individual participants and a repeated-measures ANOVA framework, but treatment assignment and misinformation generation occur at the pair level. If partners' outcomes are correlated, the effective sample size is closer to the number of dyads than to the number of individuals, depending on the intraclass correlation. This likely overstates power for intervention effects.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." / "A power of 90% was assumed in both analyses." / "The option used in G*Power was ‘ANOVA: Repeated measures, within-between’."

issues.subcategory: inappropriate ANOVA for sparse bounded count data
issues.description: The primary outcomes are counts over only four discussed and four non-discussed critical items, yielding bounded discrete variables with limited variance and likely non-normal residuals. A conventional ANOVA on such counts is fragile, especially with ceiling/floor effects and unequal item difficulty. Item-level generalized mixed-effects models, binomial/multinomial models, or preregistered nonparametric approaches would better match the data structure.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details" / "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ..." / "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.subcategory: items not modeled as random effects
issues.description: The planned ANOVA aggregates over a very small fixed set of stimulus details and does not model item variability. This limits inference to the specific eight details in the Eric movie and makes the discussion effect vulnerable to item-specific difficulty. Because item identity is central to the manipulation, item-level random effects or full counterbalancing are needed for valid generalization beyond these particular items.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details" / "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.subcategory: misclassification of misinformation exposure
issues.description: The analysis plan says all discussed items will be treated as containing misinformation, even though the actual discussion may not have exposed a participant to misinformation. The partner may say 'don't know,' agree with the participant, guess the participant's version, mention neither version, or fail to communicate clearly. Classifying all discussed items as misinformation exposure introduces measurement error and can bias estimates of conformity and intervention efficacy.
issues.quote: "However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, “white mug” ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading." / "In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation"

issues.subcategory: memory conformity conflated with arbitrary partner errors
issues.description: The plan treats any partner answer inconsistent with the participant's viewed version as misinformation, including answers that do not match the partner's viewed version. This broad coding conflates true co-witness conformity to the partner's witnessed alternative with exposure to guesses or novel errors generated during discussion. These may reflect different mechanisms and should be separately coded.
issues.quote: "For example, the participant had seen a white mug and their partner had seen a green mug. All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion (green mug, violet mug, yellow mug, blue mug) are misleading the participant and will be classified as misleading."

issues.subcategory: collaborative recognition options introduce non-social misinformation
issues.description: During collaborative recall, participants see five response alternatives for each question. If the alternatives include both versions or plausible lures, the task itself introduces misinformation or cues independently of the partner's statement. This undermines the claim that misinformation is delivered through social interaction and complicates interpretation of conformity as co-witness influence.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.subcategory: unclear handling of disagreements during collaborative recall
issues.description: The procedure notes that both responses will be documented if participants fail to agree, but the analysis does not specify how disagreement trials will be coded. A participant may be exposed to misinformation even without agreement, and the final response may depend on whether the participant initially resisted or yielded. Without rules for disagreement, speaking order, and partner response coding, the primary exposure variable is ambiguous.
issues.quote: "If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded."

issues.subcategory: no coding protocol or inter-rater reliability
issues.description: If the final test is open-ended, coding responses as correct, misinformation-consistent, other, or omissions requires judgment. The manuscript does not specify coding rules, coder blinding to condition, number of coders, adjudication procedures, or inter-rater reliability. This is especially problematic because intervention effects could be small and coding bias could be condition-dependent.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" / "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ..."

issues.subcategory: lack of experimenter blinding
issues.description: The experimenter appears to administer condition-specific interventions, DRM feedback, motivation, and final testing. No blinding or standardization procedures are described. Knowledge of condition can influence tone, encouragement, handling of questions, timing, and scoring, introducing expectancy effects.
issues.quote: "At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants" / "Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test"

issues.subcategory: interventions not matched on demand characteristics
issues.description: The three interventions differ not only in the intended theoretical active ingredient but also in explicitness, demand, emotional content, instructions, and perceived relevance to the memory test. The extended warning and demonstration/motivation conditions explicitly tell participants not to rely on the partner, whereas education and control do not. Any differences could reflect demand compliance or response strategy rather than reduced memory conformity.
issues.quote: "The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner." / "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.subcategory: interventions not matched on activity and cognitive load
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition includes an active DRM memory task, worksheet, feedback, and a motivational podcast, whereas other conditions primarily involve listening to podcasts. This introduces differences in retention interval, interference, engagement, fatigue, arousal, and experimenter contact, any of which could affect final memory performance independently of the intended intervention.
issues.quote: "First ... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used" / "The subjects will also receive a worksheet to write down all the words they remember from the lists." / "Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast"

issues.subcategory: DRM task does not operationalize co-witness influence
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention is justified as demonstrating vulnerability to influence, but DRM false recall is an internally generated associative false-memory paradigm, not social co-witness misinformation. Vulnerability to critical lures may not map onto vulnerability to social memory conformity. The construct being demonstrated is therefore only loosely related to the construct the intervention is supposed to target.
issues.quote: "in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used"

issues.subcategory: compound interventions prevent attribution to named mechanisms
issues.description: Each intervention bundles multiple components. The extended warning includes warning, source-monitoring instruction, education about misinformation, confidence framing, examples, and enlightenment. Demonstration and motivation combines DRM feedback, emotional legal consequences, and explicit instructions. Because components are not isolated, the study cannot determine which mechanism caused any effect, despite making mechanism-specific claims.
issues.quote: "the following ideas were included ... a clear warning ... an extensive lecture ... information about the possibility of confusing sources ... information that many people ... decide to give answers consistent with external sources ... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception"

issues.subcategory: normative influence incorrectly ruled out
issues.description: The manuscript asserts that normative influence is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. This is conceptually too strong. Normative pressure can operate during the collaborative discussion, through desire to agree, public commitment, partner dominance, or concern about later consistency, and can affect subsequent individual reports. The design does not measure or eliminate these processes.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing."

issues.subcategory: awareness-of-discrepancy hypothesis not measured
issues.description: A central theoretical prediction is that interventions should work especially for participants aware of discrepancies between their memory and the partner's statements. However, the planned procedure does not include a source-monitoring or discrepancy-awareness measure before the final test, so the proposed moderator cannot be tested directly. This weakens the link between theory and operationalization.
issues.quote: "we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies."

issues.subcategory: mechanistic causal claims without mediator measures
issues.description: The manuscript makes causal claims about interventions causing participants to abandon the consistency assumption, inspect memories more closely, improve source monitoring, or rely on their own recollections. Yet the design appears to measure only final memory reports and confidence, with no direct measures of consistency assumptions, source monitoring, perceived partner credibility, motivation, or metamemory change. This prevents mechanistic inference.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies between their memories and information provided by the partner, and consequently cause them to rely on their own knowledge"

issues.subcategory: no clearly specified primary outcome
issues.description: The analysis plan lists multiple dependent variables and indices but does not designate a single primary endpoint for testing the intervention hypotheses. Depending on whether the outcome is correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, overall answers, accuracy, or confidence, conclusions could differ. This creates researcher degrees of freedom and inflates false-positive risk.
issues.quote: "We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions."

issues.subcategory: multiple comparisons without correction plan
issues.description: The study has four groups, several outcomes, and planned follow-up comparisons. The manuscript does not specify familywise-error or false-discovery control, a hierarchical testing strategy, or which contrasts are confirmatory versus exploratory. This raises the probability of spurious findings.
issues.quote: "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed." / "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

issues.subcategory: one-tailed directional tests despite plausible opposite effects
issues.description: The manuscript plans directional significance tests while explicitly acknowledging that some interventions may increase suggestibility. One-tailed tests are inappropriate when theoretically plausible effects exist in both directions, and they can bias interpretation of unexpected harmful effects.
issues.quote: "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed." / "If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible." / "it could even increase suggestibility"

issues.subcategory: unclear confirmatory versus exploratory analyses
issues.description: The manuscript describes several exploratory analyses but does not clearly separate them from confirmatory tests or specify how exploratory findings will be labeled and controlled. The DRM predictor analysis is especially ambiguous because the DRM task is administered only in one intervention condition.
issues.quote: "As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique."

issues.subcategory: questionable effect-size synthesis for power analysis
issues.description: The power analysis combines two very discrepant prior effects using a random-effects synthesis and converts the resulting Hedges' g to Cohen's f without specifying whether the source effects are paired-sample standardized differences, independent-group effects, or adjusted effects. With only two studies and large heterogeneity, the synthesized effect and conversion are unstable and may not correspond to the planned ANOVA interaction or count outcomes.
issues.quote: "The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 ... and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74" / "Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57."

issues.subcategory: effect-size conventions used instead of substantively justified target
issues.description: For the key intervention effect, the manuscript acknowledges that no comparable data exist and then relies on conventional small/medium/large f values. Conventional values may not reflect the smallest effect of theoretical or practical interest, especially in forensic applications. The chosen sample therefore does not establish whether the study is powered for a meaningful reduction in memory conformity.
issues.quote: "no data exists that would allow the expected effect size to be estimated" / "the power analysis was done in the standard way for a small, medium, and large effect, according to the existing conventions"

issues.subcategory: pair composition and familiarity not controlled
issues.description: Memory conformity is known to vary with familiarity, trust, status, gender composition, dominance, and relationship between co-witnesses. The manuscript does not specify whether participants are strangers, whether acquaintances are excluded, how dyads are formed, or whether pair-level characteristics will be measured or balanced. This threatens internal validity and may increase unexplained variance.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet." / "the participants (always a pair of them) will watch the movie"

issues.subcategory: no control for speaking order or dominance in discussion
issues.description: Collaborative recall outcomes can depend on who speaks first, confidence, assertiveness, and dominance. The manuscript records audio but does not specify coding or controlling for these variables. Intervention effects could be confounded if interventions alter assertiveness or response criterion rather than memory.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer." / "The discussion will be audio recorded."

issues.subcategory: randomization and allocation concealment underspecified
issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly assigned to conditions but does not describe the randomization method, allocation concealment, blocking, stratification, or balancing by movie version, glasses orientation, participant position, or dyad characteristics. These details are needed to assess selection bias and replicability.
issues.quote: "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: (1) Extended warning, (2) Education about memory, (3) Demonstration and motivation, and (4) control condition."

issues.subcategory: counterbalancing of movie versions and participant positions missing
issues.description: The MORI technique requires assigning each member of a pair to one of two movie versions through polarized glasses. The manuscript does not specify how versions, glasses, seating side, or projector polarization are assigned and counterbalanced. Without this, version-specific or position-specific artifacts could confound responses.
issues.quote: "each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie"

issues.subcategory: insufficient perceptual screening and manipulation checks
issues.description: The stimuli include color and visual details, and the procedure depends on participants seeing only one movie version through polarized glasses. The manuscript does not specify screening for color blindness, visual acuity, hearing, Polish comprehension, or checks that participants did not see ghost images or notice dual projection. Failures would compromise the manipulation and outcome validity.
issues.quote: "e.g., in the first version, Eric is trying on a black hat, whereas in the second version the hat is red" / "Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side)"

issues.subcategory: no manipulation checks for intervention comprehension
issues.description: The study assumes that participants understand and internalize the warning, education, and motivation content, but no comprehension, attention, or perceived credibility checks are described. Without such checks, null effects could reflect failed delivery rather than ineffective interventions, and positive effects could reflect demand awareness.
issues.quote: "Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast" / "those in in the ‘Education about memory’ group will listen to the podcast" / "Afterwards, the participants will be motivated to resist illegitimate influences."

issues.subcategory: hypothesis awareness assessed only after outcome
issues.description: Participants are asked after the final memory test what they think the purpose was, but the interventions, especially warning and motivation, may make the hypothesis transparent before the test. The manuscript does not specify how suspected purpose or awareness of deception will be used in confirmatory analyses. Demand characteristics may therefore masquerade as reduced memory conformity.
issues.quote: "Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance."

issues.subcategory: missing-data handling absent
issues.description: The only exclusion rule concerns technical problems. There is no plan for participant withdrawal, incomplete responses, skipped confidence ratings, failure to follow instructions, unusable audio, no-shows that leave unpaired participants, or one member of a dyad being excluded. Because the study is dyadic, missingness in one participant affects the partner's exposure and the unit of analysis.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.subcategory: exclusion criteria too vague
issues.description: Excluding participants for 'technical problems' is underspecified. Technical problems could include projector misalignment, audio failure, participant peeking, suspicion, recording failure, or timing errors. Without objective criteria and a rule for dyad-level exclusion, exclusions could be applied flexibly after seeing data.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.subcategory: materials insufficiently specified for replication
issues.description: The podcasts, DRM lists, exact wording of educational content, control content, final memory questions, collaborative questions, and Polish translations are not provided in full. Approximate descriptions are insufficient for replication, especially because subtle wording differences can strongly affect warning and misinformation effects.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" / "The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" / "Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect."

issues.subcategory: control condition may not be inert or matched
issues.description: The control podcast concerns soft skills related to social attitudes, which may itself affect social orientation, compliance, confidence, or interpersonal reasoning. It is also not clearly matched to the active conditions on memory relevance, threat, demand, or legal salience. This weakens causal attribution of between-group differences to the intended intervention components.
issues.quote: "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.subcategory: accuracy differences may reflect response criterion rather than memory protection
issues.description: The interventions, especially legal motivation and warnings, may encourage participants to withhold uncertain answers or avoid partner-consistent responses strategically. The planned outcomes include overall number of answers but do not specify how response criterion, omissions, or 'don't know' responses will be incorporated into the primary inference. Apparent accuracy gains could reflect conservatism rather than improved memory or reduced conformity.
issues.quote: "The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner." / "Four indices will be derived ... (4) the overall number of answers."

issues.subcategory: relative efficacy predictions weakly grounded
issues.description: The predicted ordering of interventions relies on persuasion-resistance research involving advertisements and authority cues, not eyewitness co-witness memory contamination. The theoretical transfer from resistance to illegitimate authority in advertisements to resistance to memory conformity is underdeveloped, making the ordered hypothesis speculative.
issues.quote: "Based on the research of Sagarin et al. (2002), we tentatively assume that the most effective technique in reducing the memory conformity effect will be Demonstration and motivation"

issues.subcategory: metamemory claims not operationalized
issues.description: The Education about memory condition is claimed to enhance memory monitoring, sense of memory efficacy, and affect, but these constructs are not measured. Thus the study cannot determine whether the intervention changed metamemory or whether such changes mediated resistance to misinformation.
issues.quote: "We assume that the lecture will also enhance memory monitoring, sense of memory efficacy or even memory-related affect."

issues.subcategory: restricted convenience sample overextended to justice settings
issues.description: The sample is a convenience sample aged 16–35 recruited via media/internet, yet the framing emphasizes eyewitness testimony and justice systems broadly. Older adults, children, actual witnesses, stressed witnesses, police interviewees, and courtroom contexts may differ substantially in memory, social influence, motivation, and stakes. These limits need explicit acknowledgment before practical recommendations.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet." / "research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems"

issues.subcategory: minor participants and consent procedures not addressed
issues.description: The inclusion range begins at age 16, which may involve minors depending on jurisdiction. The manuscript does not describe parental consent, assent, ethical safeguards for deception, or whether minors will be analyzed separately. This is a reporting and ethical completeness gap.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.subcategory: age-restriction rationale does not ensure age matching
issues.description: The manuscript restricts age to 16–35 to avoid very young participants discussing with elderly participants, but this does not prevent meaningful age/status differences within dyads, nor does it specify age matching. A 16-year-old paired with a 35-year-old may still experience authority or dominance differences relevant to conformity.
issues.quote: "The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one, which would possibly activate some confounding factors"

issues.subcategory: no plan for confidence analyses despite collection
issues.description: The procedure collects confidence ratings for every final answer, but the analysis plan does not specify confirmatory or exploratory analyses for confidence, calibration, or confidence-accuracy relationships. Given the theoretical focus on lack of confidence and reliance on one's own memory, omitting a planned confidence analysis is a missed validity check.
issues.quote: "for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100%"

issues.subcategory: potential contamination after intervention not controlled
issues.description: The final test occurs after both members of a dyad receive condition procedures, but the manuscript does not state whether participants are separated, prohibited from communicating, or tested in isolation. Any post-intervention conversation could create additional contamination or allow participants to coordinate answers.
issues.quote: "Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test of the original material"

issues.subcategory: gatekeeping omnibus interaction may not match planned hypotheses
issues.description: The hypotheses concern specific treatment-versus-control reductions in the discussion effect and an ordered comparison among interventions. Requiring a significant omnibus interaction before follow-up pairwise comparisons can reduce power for the planned contrasts and does not directly test the ordered hypotheses. The contrast structure should be preregistered rather than contingent on an omnibus test.
issues.quote: "The hypothesis concerning the efficacy of the methods for reducing the memory conformity effect will be verified by means of analyzing the interaction" / "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed."

issues.subcategory: collaborative and final question order not specified
issues.description: Question order can affect recall, discussion dynamics, and later memory. The manuscript does not specify whether collaborative and final test question orders are fixed, randomized, counterbalanced, or matched across participants. This omission reduces replicability and may introduce order confounds.
issues.quote: "The test will comprise 12 questions" / "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions"

issues.subcategory: condition naming inconsistency
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition is later called the DRM group. Although minor, inconsistent labels can create ambiguity about whether DRM is the whole condition or only one component of it, especially because the DRM result is later proposed as a predictor.
issues.quote: "(3) Demonstration and motivation" / "Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback"
